newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wheat prices ease as weather alarms abate.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wheat prices ease as weather alarms abate.

text.p: Wheat prices tended lower on Tuesday as concerns about the impact on crops of freak weather babated.
May wheat futures on the Chicago Board of Trade slipped below $4.00 per bushel for the first time since April 11, touching $3.96.
They "spiked" up to $4.59 on April 21 after floods and a cold snap in the United States and worries about a prolonged dry spell in western Europe.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture now says 13 percent of U.S. spring wheat had been planted by last Sunday, up from five percent a week earlier although still behind 21 percent a year ago.

Traders also noted good rains in France. French wheat prices also eased on Monday on improved prospects for the 1997 harvest after weekend rain and forecasts for more rain and cooler temperatures in the next few days.
The July CBOT wheat contract was somewhat firmer on Tuesday than the expiring May at around $4.05 per bushel but it was nonetheless also well down on values around $4.50 seen in mid-April.
U.S. traders noted reports that leading consultants Sparks Companies had projected U.S. hard red winter wheat production at 966 million bushels, a total higher than most had anticipated.

"It (weakness) is partly Sparks but it is also a general perception the crops are looking better in several areas," one dealer said, noting that concern about droughts in both Europe and Australia had lessened following recent rains.

Elsewhere in commodity markets, coffee prices were firm but the benchmark New York arabica contract remained below a contract high at $2.25 per pound set last week before profit-taking blunted a vigorous new rally.
The rally on arabica coffee, in which prices have doubled since late 1996, reignited last week on concerns about tight Latin American supply and the onset of the Brazilian frost season.
A threat of a new truckers strike in Colombia supported coffee prices on Tuesday.

London futures for robusta beans, used in making soluble or instant coffee, are also strong -- up by one-third since the start of 1997. They rose above $1,700 per tonne on the July contract on Tuesday.

London gold prices firmed but later surrendered some of the gains made on news that claims by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd for its gold discovery at Busang in Indonesia were based on data that had been falsified.
The gold market was "too big and it has been around too long" to reel under one mine failure, a London dealer said.

Bullion fixed at $342.45 an ounce in London's afternoon, compared with Friday values around $340. But with stock markets rushing to new peaks most dealers were sceptical about a continued rally in gold.

Crude oil prices were somewhat firmer on good heating oil demand. Cold weather has hit Europe and the benchmark Brent Blend of North Sea crude for July traded in London just above $18 per barrel, up some 25 cents from last week.
